elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 10.4 is left intact: "All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property" and Developed Software "shall be the property of M&I". The redline does not disturb M&I's ownership, consistent with targeting the fallback.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant: "M&I grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business." Note the residual tension with 17.2's "during the Term" wording is addressed only by a carve-out citing "Section 10.5", which is not a numbered clause in the rendered text (see intent reasons).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" — "irrevocable" appears expressly in the inserted grant; 17.2 is conformed by an express carve-out for the licensed rights.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears expressly in the inserted grant of the licence to the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" appears expressly in the inserted grant; no fee or further consideration is attached to the licence.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business" — use and modify rights are express and scoped to Customer's business, and "Developed Software" is the defined deliverable created by M&I under 10.4.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "...and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business" — the sublicence right is express in the inserted grant; the Article 23 no-sublicence restriction concerns the separate IBS source-code licence, not this grant.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 17.4 as amended: "...other than for the purposes contemplated by this Agreement, provided that M&I shall use Customer Data solely to provide the Services...". The proviso overrides the broader "purposes contemplated" permission for Customer Data (defined in 17.1 as any and all data submitted to or received by M&I on Customer's behalf), and no distribution/resale right over Customer Data is retained.

elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: 10.4 retained unchanged: "Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I". Customer ownership is not established (deliberate, as the fallback level was targeted).

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language of any kind is added; M&I retains title and may still "make such Developed Software available to any of its other customers".

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 10.4 and 17.1/17.2 preserve M&I's ownership of its programs, know-how, software, systems and documentation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The inserted grant is "perpetual" and covers the Developed Software in which any embedded M&I IP sits; the 17.2 acknowledgement is carved out accordingly (subject to the numbering defect noted).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "irrevocable" appears expressly in the inserted grant covering the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" appears expressly in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: 17.1 left intact: "Customer shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data and other Confidential Information ... regardless of whether such data is maintained on magnetic tape, magnetic disk, or any other storage or processing device."

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same amended 17.4 proviso: "M&I shall use Customer Data solely to provide the Services".

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no joint-ownership language exists in 10.4, 17.1, 17.2 or 17.4, and the redline creates none, so nothing needs deleting.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on its face: the inserted grant supplies perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free rights to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business; M&I's ownership of its programs and know-how is retained (fallback element 1); and amended 17.4 confines M&I's use of Customer Data to providing the Services.

Preferred level correctly fails: no Customer ownership of, or assignment of, work product created for Customer — the drafter's choice to target the fallback rather than reverse 10.4's ownership direction is a defensible level selection, not an omission.

Intent defect to repair: the inserted licence paragraph is rendered as an unnumbered clause ("License to Developed Software.") while the conforming edit in 17.2 carves out rights "as expressly licensed to Customer under Section 10.5". As rendered, Section 10.5 does not exist, leaving a dangling cross-reference; the ineffective carve-out means 17.2's retained "no rights ... except with respect to Customer's use of the same during the Term" contradicts the perpetual, irrevocable licence. Fix: expressly number the inserted clause as "10.5 License to Developed Software." (or repoint the 17.2 carve-out to the actual clause number).

Minimality holds: three operations, each tied to a selected element — (i) the grant itself, (ii) the narrow 17.2 conforming carve-out needed to avoid a contradictory retained sentence, and (iii) the 17.4 Customer Data proviso. No survival tail, expense language, damages categories, procedures or extra restrictions were added, the mutual confidentiality standard and the 10.4 refund/credit mechanic are preserved, and no favourable existing wording (including 17.1's sole-ownership sentence) was deleted.

No walk-away trigger remains: nothing assigns Customer IP or Customer Data to M&I and no joint ownership is created; M&I's ability to resell Developed Software to other customers survives but is acceptable at the fallback because Customer now holds an unrestricted business licence.
